domain_label: Ontology Engineering — Knowledge Representation & Ontology Engineering subdomain
purpose: Provide a session-bounded, subdomain-grain ontology of Ontology Engineering work units (scope/requirements, methodology selection, competency questions, reuse and resource selection, foundational/upper-ontology commitment, conceptualization, class taxonomy and property modeling, logical axioms, design patterns, modularization and imports, naming/IRI policy, representation language and OWL profile, population and learning, consistency reasoning, pitfall and coverage evaluation, matching/alignment, documentation, and governance/versioning) to plan, evaluate, sequence, validate, and lock the construction or adoption of ontologies for finding, retrieving, evaluating, and synthesizing authoritative knowledge.
assumptions: Parent domain is knowledge_representation_and_ontology_engineering; this KB models the Ontology Engineering subdomain at subdomain grain.
No observed dataset, benchmark, or expert-judgment input was supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Each node is a single ontology-engineering work unit, method, or decision area sized for one heavy reasoning session.
Intended uses, scope, and competency questions are parameters the workflow profiles before locking structure.
Both build-new and reuse/adopt paths are in scope; OWL 2 with an explicit profile is the default representation target.
exclusions: Generic knowledge-representation formalism research (rule languages, non-OWL logics) beyond representation-language selection.
Reasoner algorithm internals and tableau optimization (consumed only as a reasoning capability).
Domain-specific subject content of any particular ontology (the actual concepts of one discipline).
Full information-retrieval/search-engine ranking and indexing (covered by other KBs).
Knowledge-graph data engineering and ETL pipelines except as ontology population inputs.

competency_questions.question: What scope, intended uses, stakeholders, and build-vs-reuse framing bound this ontology effort?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OE_SCOPE_REQ outputs an ORSD, scope statement, and build-vs-reuse framing

competency_questions.question: Which ontology engineering methodology, lifecycle, roles, and gates govern the build?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OE_METHODOLOGY selects a methodology, NeOn scenarios, and a role/activity matrix

competency_questions.question: What competency questions must the ontology answer and is their coverage demonstrated by executed queries?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OE_COMPETENCY_Q and OE_CQ_COVERAGE present with executed coverage results

competency_questions.question: Which external ontologies and resources are reused, and how was reuse fitness and license evaluated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OE_REUSE_SELECT outputs a reuse set, fitness report, and license assessment

competency_questions.question: Which foundational/upper ontology and ontological commitments are adopted and documented?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OE_FOUNDATIONAL outputs an upper-ontology decision and commitment record

competency_questions.question: What domain conceptualization (concepts, informal definitions, candidate relations) underlies the model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OE_CONCEPTUALIZE outputs a concept list, glossary, and candidate relations

competency_questions.question: How is the class taxonomy structured (subsumption, disjointness, strategy) to support inference?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OE_CLASS_HIERARCHY outputs an acyclic hierarchy with disjointness axioms

competency_questions.question: How are object/data properties modeled (domains, ranges, characteristics, hierarchy)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OE_PROPERTIES outputs property definitions with justified domain/range and characteristics

competency_questions.question: Which logical axioms and restrictions capture the intended formal semantics?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OE_AXIOMS_RESTRICT outputs restriction axioms traceable to CQs or commitments

competency_questions.question: Which ontology design patterns and anti-patterns apply to recurring modeling problems?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OE_DESIGN_PATTERNS outputs instantiated patterns and anti-pattern notes

competency_questions.question: How is the ontology modularized and how are import closure and IRI/naming policy controlled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OE_MODULARIZATION and OE_NAMING_IRI output an import graph and IRI policy

competency_questions.question: Which representation language/OWL profile is chosen and is the ontology logically consistent within it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OE_SERIALIZE_LANG, OE_CONSISTENCY, OE_PITFALL_SCAN present with profile and consistency reports

competency_questions.question: How is the ontology populated with instances and what ontology-learning output is curated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OE_POPULATION outputs a curated, confidence-scored ABox and learned axioms

competency_questions.question: Is the ontology aligned to external ontologies, documented, published, and governed for reuse and maintenance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OE_MATCHING_ALIGN, OE_DOCUMENTATION, OE_GOVERNANCE present with alignment, docs, and policy

glossary.definition: a formal, shared specification of a conceptualization: classes, relations, and axioms
a question the ontology must answer, used as a functional requirement and test oracle
a domain-independent foundational ontology fixing top-level categories (BFO, DOLCE, SUMO)
a reusable modeling solution to a recurring problem (content, structural, logical)
a self-contained, reusable subset of an ontology with a defined interface
an OWL class expression constraining members via a property (existential, universal, cardinality)
a tractable sublanguage of OWL 2 (EL, QL, RL) trading expressivity for reasoning complexity
logical property that an ontology has at least one model (no contradiction)
a common modeling worst-practice detectable by tools such as OOPS!
computing correspondences (alignments) between entities of different ontologies
adding instances (ABox) to an ontology's schema (TBox)
semi-automatic extraction of concepts, relations, or axioms from data
an Internationalized Resource Identifier naming an ontology entity, ideally stable and dereferenceable
Ontology Requirements Specification Document capturing purpose, scope, and competency questions

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established ontology engineering literature and practice (Staab & Studer, Handbook on Ontologies 2009; Allemang & Hendler, Semantic Web for the Working Ontologist 2011; Noy & McGuinness, Ontology Development 101; NeOn and METHONTOLOGY methodologies); no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Establish the ontology's intended use, scope, stakeholders, and functional requirements that justify and bound the engineering effort.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when intended use, stakeholder set, or domain boundary shift materially

pros.claim: prevents engineering the wrong artifact for the task
pros.example: building a heavyweight axiomatized ontology when a lightweight taxonomy met the need

cons.claim: scope errors propagate into every downstream modeling and reuse decision
cons.example: under-scoping omits a subdomain that later forces a costly ontology split

failure_modes: scope driven by data not by use cases
ignoring reusable existing ontologies
acceptance_tests: ORSD names intended uses and stakeholders
scope statement bounds in/out concepts explicitly

nodes.definition: Select and instantiate an ontology engineering methodology (METHONTOLOGY, NeOn, Ontology Development 101, Uschold-King) appropriate to scope, team, and reuse strategy.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when team composition, reuse needs, or scope size changes the suitable lifecycle

pros.claim: gives repeatable activities, roles, and gates instead of improvisation
pros.example: NeOn scenario 3 routes the project to reuse-and-reengineer existing resources

cons.claim: a heavy methodology can over-burden a small lightweight effort
cons.example: running full METHONTOLOGY ceremony for a 50-class glossary

failure_modes: choosing methodology by familiarity not fit
skipping methodology entirely
acceptance_tests: selected methodology mapped to NeOn scenarios
lifecycle activities assigned to roles

nodes.definition: Elicit and formalize competency questions that the ontology must answer, serving as functional requirements and test oracles.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when use cases or required answers change, invalidating existing CQs

pros.claim: turns vague scope into testable functional requirements
pros.example: the CQ which drugs interact with warfarin fixes needed classes and relations

cons.claim: poorly written CQs over- or under-constrain the model
cons.example: an ambiguous CQ leads to modeling concepts never actually queried

failure_modes: CQs too generic to test
skipping formalization so CQs cannot be checked
acceptance_tests: each CQ is answerable by a planned query pattern
every CQ links to at least one requirement

nodes.definition: Search, evaluate, and select existing ontologies, vocabularies, and non-ontological resources to reuse rather than build from scratch.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a reused resource is deprecated, relicensed, or a better candidate appears

pros.claim: reduces cost and improves interoperability via shared semantics
pros.example: reusing FOAF and Dublin Core instead of reinventing person/document terms

cons.claim: reusing a misaligned resource imports unwanted commitments
cons.example: importing an ontology whose class semantics conflict with the domain

failure_modes: reuse without evaluating fitness
ignoring license or maintenance risk
acceptance_tests: each reused resource passes a fitness check against CQs
license and maintenance status recorded

nodes.definition: Decide whether and which foundational/upper ontology (BFO, DOLCE, SUMO) to commit to, fixing top-level ontological choices.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when interoperability targets demand a different top-level or a commitment proves untenable

pros.claim: enforces consistent top-level categories and eases cross-domain integration
pros.example: aligning to BFO lets independently built biomedical ontologies interoperate

cons.claim: a wrong or heavy upper-ontology commitment is costly and hard to reverse
cons.example: forcing a 4D perdurantist model onto an inherently 3D domain

failure_modes: committing to an upper ontology that mismatches domain
ignoring upper ontology then retrofitting it
acceptance_tests: upper-ontology choice justified against interoperability targets
ontological commitments documented and consistent
revisit_triggers: new interoperability partner with different top-level

nodes.definition: Extract domain terms and produce a shared conceptualization: concept list, informal definitions, and concept-relation candidates before formalization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when corpus or expert input introduces new concepts or invalidates definitions

pros.claim: builds shared agreement on meaning before committing to logic
pros.example: glossary review surfaces two experts using one term for different concepts

cons.claim: informal definitions can hide disagreements that surface only in axioms
cons.example: a definition agreed informally proves logically inconsistent later

failure_modes: mixing terms (lexical) with concepts (semantic)
skipping informal agreement and formalizing prematurely
acceptance_tests: each concept has an informal definition reviewed by an expert
term-to-concept map has no unresolved homonyms

nodes.definition: Model the class taxonomy (subsumption hierarchy) using a defensible strategy (top-down, bottom-up, middle-out) and disjointness.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new classes or disjointness constraints change the subsumption structure

pros.claim: a clean subsumption hierarchy drives inference and reuse
pros.example: declaring disjoint sibling classes lets a reasoner detect contradictory instances

cons.claim: taxonomy mistakes (isA vs instanceOf, multiple inheritance abuse) corrupt inference
cons.example: modeling a part-of relation as subClassOf produces false subsumptions

failure_modes: confusing isA with part-of or instance-of
missing disjointness so reasoner cannot catch errors
acceptance_tests: subClassOf chains are acyclic and meaningful
disjointness declared where siblings are mutually exclusive

nodes.definition: Model object and data properties: domains, ranges, characteristics (functional, transitive, inverse), and property hierarchies.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when CQs require new relations or property characteristics change inference

pros.claim: correct domains/ranges and characteristics enable rich inference
pros.example: declaring hasPart transitive lets queries traverse whole-part chains

cons.claim: over-tight domain/range axioms cause unintended classification of instances
cons.example: an over-constrained domain forces an instance into an unwanted class

failure_modes: overusing domain/range as constraints (they entail, not check)
ignoring inverse/functional characteristics needed by CQs
acceptance_tests: each CQ-required relation exists with justified domain/range
property characteristics validated against intended inference

nodes.definition: Author logical restriction axioms (existential, universal, cardinality, equivalence, defined classes) to capture intended formal semantics.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when reasoning reveals under- or over-constrained semantics

pros.claim: axioms make implicit knowledge inferable and enable defined-class classification
pros.example: an equivalent-class axiom auto-classifies instances as HighRiskPatient

cons.claim: incautious axioms cause unsatisfiable classes or unintended entailments
cons.example: an existential plus universal restriction makes a class unsatisfiable

failure_modes: confusing someValuesFrom with allValuesFrom
over-axiomatizing beyond what CQs require
acceptance_tests: reasoner reports no unsatisfiable classes
each axiom traces to a CQ or commitment
revisit_triggers: new CQ needs a defined class

nodes.definition: Apply content, structural, and logical ontology design patterns to recurring modeling problems for quality and reuse.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a recurring modeling problem lacks a matching pattern or an anti-pattern is detected

pros.claim: reusing proven patterns improves quality and avoids known anti-patterns
pros.example: using the participation content pattern for events instead of ad-hoc relations

cons.claim: forcing a pattern that does not fit adds accidental complexity
cons.example: instantiating an n-ary relation pattern where a simple property sufficed

failure_modes: pattern misapplication
reinventing solutions a pattern already solves
acceptance_tests: each used pattern matches its documented problem
no listed anti-patterns present

nodes.definition: Partition the ontology into modules and manage import closure, ensuring cohesion, low coupling, and controlled dependency.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when import closure grows unmanageable or a module's cohesion degrades

pros.claim: modularization enables independent reuse and limits change blast radius
pros.example: extracting a units-of-measure module lets other ontologies import only it

cons.claim: uncontrolled imports pull in transitive axioms that bloat or break reasoning
cons.example: importing a full upper ontology to reuse three classes slows the reasoner

failure_modes: import-closure explosion
modules with high coupling and low cohesion
acceptance_tests: import graph is acyclic and minimal
each module has a documented interface and purpose

nodes.definition: Define naming conventions and IRI/URI minting policy to ensure stable, dereferenceable, and consistent identifiers.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when namespace policy changes or identifier collisions/instability appear

pros.claim: stable dereferenceable IRIs make the ontology citable and linkable
pros.example: using PURLs so term IRIs survive server moves

cons.claim: reusing or changing IRIs breaks downstream references silently
cons.example: minting a new IRI for an existing concept fragments the linked-data graph

failure_modes: reusing a retired IRI for a new concept
unstable, non-dereferenceable IRIs
acceptance_tests: IRI policy guarantees persistence and uniqueness
no IRI is reused for a different concept

nodes.definition: Choose the representation language and OWL profile (RDFS, OWL 2 DL/EL/QL/RL) and serialization that meet reasoning and scalability needs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when reasoning performance or scalability needs change the viable profile

pros.claim: matching OWL profile to needs balances expressivity and tractable reasoning
pros.example: choosing OWL 2 EL for a large biomedical ontology to keep classification polynomial

cons.claim: over-expressive profiles make reasoning intractable at scale
cons.example: using full OWL 2 DL with axioms that blow up classification time

failure_modes: choosing a profile incompatible with required axioms
ignoring reasoner support for the profile
acceptance_tests: chosen profile supports all authored axioms
reasoner classifies within the performance budget
revisit_triggers: axiom set leaves the chosen profile

nodes.definition: Populate the ontology with instances (ABox) and apply ontology learning to semi-automatically extract concepts, relations, or instances from data.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when source data changes or extraction precision/recall degrades

pros.claim: learning and population scale the ontology beyond manual authoring
pros.example: relation extraction proposes thousands of candidate gene-disease links

cons.claim: learned/extracted axioms inject noise and require human curation
cons.example: an extractor asserts false instance memberships that corrupt inference

failure_modes: accepting learned axioms without curation
population that violates schema constraints
acceptance_tests: learned additions are confidence-scored and reviewed before commit
populated ABox passes consistency check

nodes.definition: Run a reasoner to check consistency, satisfiability, and classification, detecting logical defects before evaluation and release.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when any axiom changes, requiring re-running the reasoner

pros.claim: reasoning catches logical defects that human review misses
pros.example: reasoner reveals an unsatisfiable class caused by conflicting restrictions

cons.claim: reasoner output (especially inferred hierarchy) can surprise modelers
cons.example: an unintended equivalence between two classes is only found via classification

failure_modes: releasing without a consistency check
ignoring unsatisfiable classes as harmless
acceptance_tests: ontology is consistent and has no unsatisfiable classes
every unexpected entailment is explained and accepted

nodes.definition: Scan the ontology with quality/pitfall tools (OOPS!) and quality criteria to detect modeling pitfalls and worst practices.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the ontology changes or new pitfall categories are published

pros.claim: automated pitfall scanning catches common worst practices cheaply
pros.example: OOPS! flags missing inverse relationships and unconnected classes

cons.claim: pitfall tools produce false positives needing triage
cons.example: a flagged missing domain is intentional for a generic property

failure_modes: treating every pitfall as a blocker
skipping the scan before release
acceptance_tests: all critical-severity pitfalls resolved or justified
quality scorecard recorded

nodes.definition: Evaluate whether the ontology answers its competency questions via test queries, measuring functional coverage and accuracy.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when CQs change or model changes affect answerability

pros.claim: CQ-based evaluation directly tests fitness for intended use
pros.example: a query for a key CQ returns empty, exposing a missing relation

cons.claim: writing faithful test queries for vague CQs is hard
cons.example: a CQ phrased ambiguously yields a query that does not test the real need

failure_modes: declaring coverage without executing queries
tests that do not actually exercise the CQ
acceptance_tests: every CQ has an executed test query with a recorded result
coverage gaps logged with remediation
revisit_triggers: model change affects a previously-passing query

nodes.definition: Compute and curate correspondences between this ontology and external ontologies for integration and interoperability.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a matched ontology changes version or a wrong correspondence is found

pros.claim: alignment enables data integration across independently built ontologies
pros.example: an equivalence alignment lets two product catalogs be queried as one

cons.claim: automatic matchers produce false correspondences that propagate errors
cons.example: a high-similarity but wrong equivalence merges two distinct concepts

failure_modes: accepting matcher output without curation
using equivalence where only subsumption holds
acceptance_tests: each accepted correspondence is human-validated with a relation type
alignment introduces no inconsistency when imported

nodes.definition: Produce human- and machine-readable documentation (annotations, definitions, HTML docs) and publish the ontology for discovery and reuse.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the ontology changes or documentation drifts from the artifact

pros.claim: good documentation is decisive for reuse and adoption
pros.example: clear rdfs:comment definitions let outside teams reuse terms correctly

cons.claim: documentation drifts from the ontology if not regenerated
cons.example: stale HTML docs describe classes that were renamed

failure_modes: publishing without definitions or license
docs that lag the ontology version
acceptance_tests: every class/property has a label and definition
published metadata includes license and provenance

nodes.definition: Establish change control, versioning, deprecation policy, and maintenance process for the ontology lifecycle after release.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a release introduces breaking changes or deprecation needs

pros.claim: governance keeps the ontology stable and trustworthy for downstream users
pros.example: a deprecation policy retires terms without breaking existing data

cons.claim: weak governance lets uncontrolled changes break consumers
cons.example: silently deleting a class breaks every dataset referencing it

failure_modes: deleting instead of deprecating
no version policy so consumers cannot pin a release
acceptance_tests: versioning and deprecation policy documented and applied
no breaking change ships without a major version increment

edges.why_related: scope and requirements determine which methodology and lifecycle fit
edges.risk_of_conflict: picking methodology before scope forces re-planning
edges.example: large reuse-heavy scope routes to NeOn reuse scenarios
edges.resolution_rule: finalize ORSD before selecting methodology

edges.why_related: scope and intended uses bound which competency questions are in scope
edges.risk_of_conflict: writing CQs without scope yields out-of-scope questions
edges.example: scope excludes billing so no billing CQs are authored
edges.resolution_rule: approve scope statement before formalizing CQs

edges.why_related: CQs define the fitness criteria for evaluating reusable resources
edges.benefit_of_coupling: reuse judged against real information needs
edges.risk_of_conflict: reusing resources before CQs risks unfit imports
edges.example: CQs requiring temporal reasoning rule out a static taxonomy
edges.resolution_rule: fix CQ set before locking the reuse decision

edges.why_related: scope boundary constrains which external resources are candidates
edges.benefit_of_coupling: reuse search is bounded and efficient
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded reuse search wastes effort
edges.example: scope to clinical domain narrows candidates to medical ontologies
edges.resolution_rule: bound reuse search to scoped domain

edges.why_related: reused resources may carry an upper ontology that constrains the foundational choice
edges.benefit_of_coupling: foundational choice consistent with reused commitments
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing an upper ontology that conflicts with reused resources forces rework
edges.example: reusing BFO-based modules pushes the project toward BFO
edges.resolution_rule: settle reuse set before finalizing upper-ontology commitment

edges.why_related: CQs seed the concepts and relations to extract during conceptualization
edges.risk_of_conflict: conceptualizing without CQs produces unused concepts
edges.example: a CQ about drug interactions seeds Drug and interactsWith
edges.resolution_rule: derive concepts from CQs and corpus together

edges.why_related: reused vocabularies supply concepts to incorporate before authoring new ones
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring reuse duplicates existing concepts
edges.example: reuse FOAF Person rather than minting a new Person concept
edges.resolution_rule: incorporate reuse concepts before authoring new ones

edges.why_related: upper-ontology categories constrain how domain classes are placed in the hierarchy
edges.benefit_of_coupling: domain classes inherit consistent top-level categories
edges.risk_of_conflict: building the hierarchy before the upper-ontology choice forces re-parenting
edges.example: BFO continuant vs occurrent split determines top-level domain branches
edges.resolution_rule: fix upper-ontology commitment before finalizing class hierarchy

edges.why_related: the concept list and informal definitions are the raw material for the class taxonomy
edges.risk_of_conflict: formalizing classes before agreeing concepts re-opens definitions
edges.example: glossary concept Vehicle becomes a class with subclasses
edges.resolution_rule: agree concepts before declaring the class hierarchy

edges.why_related: classes must exist before properties can declare their domains and ranges
edges.risk_of_conflict: declaring properties before classes leaves domains/ranges dangling
edges.example: hasManufacturer needs Product and Manufacturer classes first
edges.resolution_rule: finalize class set before fixing property domains/ranges

edges.why_related: restriction axioms reference properties, so properties must be defined first
edges.risk_of_conflict: axiomatizing before properties forces axiom rewrites
edges.example: a someValuesFrom restriction needs the hasPart property defined
edges.resolution_rule: define properties before authoring restriction axioms

edges.why_related: recurring conceptual structures indicate which design patterns apply
edges.benefit_of_coupling: patterns matched to real modeling problems
edges.risk_of_conflict: applying patterns before knowing the problem misfits them
edges.example: a recurring event-participant structure signals the participation pattern
edges.resolution_rule: identify modeling problems before instantiating patterns

edges.why_related: the class structure and reuse set determine sensible module boundaries
edges.benefit_of_coupling: modules align with cohesive concept clusters
edges.risk_of_conflict: modularizing before the hierarchy stabilizes churns module boundaries
edges.example: a coherent geo subtree becomes a geo module
edges.resolution_rule: stabilize class hierarchy before drawing module boundaries

edges.why_related: module structure determines namespace partitioning and IRI minting
edges.risk_of_conflict: minting IRIs before modules causes namespace churn
edges.example: each module gets its own namespace base IRI
edges.resolution_rule: fix module structure before locking IRI policy

edges.why_related: the authored axioms determine the required expressivity and OWL profile
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing the profile before axioms risks an incompatible profile
edges.example: cardinality plus role chains push toward OWL 2 DL
edges.resolution_rule: know the axiom set before fixing the OWL profile

edges.why_related: a stable TBox (axioms) is needed before populating instances or learning
edges.risk_of_conflict: populating before the TBox stabilizes invalidates instances
edges.example: instances added before disjointness later turn inconsistent
edges.resolution_rule: stabilize TBox before population/learning

edges.why_related: consistency checking operates on the authored axioms
edges.benefit_of_coupling: reasoner validates the real axiom set
edges.risk_of_conflict: checking before axioms are authored is meaningless
edges.example: reasoner classifies the finished TBox
edges.resolution_rule: author axioms before running the consistency check

edges.why_related: pitfall scanning evaluates the authored model for worst practices
edges.risk_of_conflict: scanning an empty model finds nothing useful
edges.example: OOPS! scans the finished ontology file
edges.resolution_rule: author the model before pitfall scanning

edges.why_related: CQ evaluation requires a consistent ontology to query meaningfully
edges.benefit_of_coupling: queries run over a consistent model
edges.risk_of_conflict: evaluating coverage on an inconsistent ontology is invalid
edges.example: an inconsistent ontology entails everything, voiding coverage tests
edges.resolution_rule: ensure consistency before measuring CQ coverage

edges.why_related: the CQ set is the test oracle for coverage evaluation
edges.risk_of_conflict: evaluating coverage without the CQ set has no oracle
edges.example: each CQ becomes a test query
edges.resolution_rule: freeze the CQ set before coverage evaluation

edges.why_related: matching aligns this ontology's classes/properties to external ones
edges.risk_of_conflict: aligning before terms stabilize churns correspondences
edges.example: aligning Product class to schema.org Product
edges.resolution_rule: stabilize core terms before computing alignments

edges.why_related: documentation should describe a consistent, validated ontology
edges.risk_of_conflict: documenting an inconsistent ontology misleads reusers
edges.example: HTML docs generated from the validated ontology
edges.resolution_rule: validate consistency before publishing documentation

edges.why_related: a documented, published release is the baseline that governance manages
edges.risk_of_conflict: governing an undocumented release leaves consumers blind
edges.example: version 1.0 docs anchor the change log
edges.resolution_rule: publish documented release before activating governance

edges.why_related: upper-ontology commitments bound which axioms are admissible
edges.benefit_of_coupling: axioms stay consistent with top-level categories
edges.risk_of_conflict: axioms that violate the upper ontology break interoperability
edges.example: BFO forbids treating a process as a continuant
edges.resolution_rule: reject axioms inconsistent with the committed upper ontology

edges.why_related: the chosen OWL profile bounds what the reasoner can decide tractably
edges.risk_of_conflict: an over-expressive profile makes consistency checking intractable
edges.example: OWL Full has no decidable reasoner
edges.resolution_rule: keep axioms within the profile the reasoner supports

edges.why_related: IRI and label policy bound how terms can be referenced in documentation
edges.risk_of_conflict: unstable IRIs make documentation links rot
edges.example: docs link to PURL-based term IRIs
edges.resolution_rule: documentation must use the policy-compliant IRIs

edges.why_related: governance deprecation rules constrain IRI reuse and retirement
edges.risk_of_conflict: reusing a deprecated IRI breaks consumers
edges.example: governance forbids reassigning a retired class IRI
edges.resolution_rule: never reuse an IRI retired by governance policy

edges.why_related: applying good patterns lowers the rate of detected pitfalls
edges.risk_of_conflict: misapplied patterns introduce their own pitfalls
edges.example: using the value-partition pattern avoids unconnected-class pitfalls
edges.resolution_rule: prefer validated patterns to reduce pitfall density

edges.why_related: reusing shared vocabularies reduces the alignment burden later
edges.risk_of_conflict: reusing divergent vocabularies increases alignment work
edges.example: reusing schema.org reduces later alignment to web data
edges.resolution_rule: reuse shared vocabularies to cut alignment cost

edges.why_related: adding instances can change reasoner results and surface inconsistencies
edges.benefit_of_coupling: population is validated against the TBox
edges.risk_of_conflict: unvalidated population can make the whole KB inconsistent
edges.example: an instance violating a disjointness axiom triggers inconsistency
edges.resolution_rule: re-run consistency after each population batch

edges.why_related: the methodology prescribes when and how CQs are captured
edges.benefit_of_coupling: CQ capture follows the chosen process
edges.risk_of_conflict: capturing CQs off-process loses methodology benefits
edges.example: NeOn schedules CQ capture in the specification activity
edges.resolution_rule: follow the methodology's CQ activity ordering

edges.why_related: resolve structural pitfalls before measuring functional coverage
edges.benefit_of_coupling: coverage tested on a clean model
edges.risk_of_conflict: measuring coverage atop pitfalls confounds results
edges.example: fix unconnected classes before running CQ queries
edges.resolution_rule: clear critical pitfalls before coverage evaluation

edges.why_related: alignments become governed artifacts maintained across versions
edges.risk_of_conflict: ungoverned alignments drift from the ontology
edges.example: alignment set is logged in the change log
edges.resolution_rule: place alignments under governance after curation

edges.why_related: consistency results can require revising the axioms that caused defects
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring reasoner feedback ships unsatisfiable classes
edges.example: an unsatisfiable class sends the modeler back to fix a restriction
edges.resolution_rule: loop until reasoner reports no unsatisfiable classes, max 5 cycles

edges.why_related: coverage gaps trigger re-conceptualization to add missing concepts/relations
edges.benefit_of_coupling: model extended to close real gaps
edges.risk_of_conflict: unaddressed gaps leave CQs unanswered
edges.example: an empty query result reveals a missing relation to add
edges.resolution_rule: loop until coverage targets met or gap accepted, max 4 cycles

edges.why_related: pitfall findings trigger targeted axiom and model fixes
edges.benefit_of_coupling: model quality raised by addressing pitfalls
edges.risk_of_conflict: unfixed critical pitfalls degrade quality
edges.example: a missing-inverse pitfall sends the modeler to add the inverse
edges.resolution_rule: loop until critical pitfalls resolved or justified, max 3 cycles

edges.why_related: both are evaluation activities but check different defect classes (worst practice vs logical)
edges.benefit_of_coupling: planners can schedule them together in an evaluation phase
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating them hides logical defects that pitfall scans miss
edges.example: a clean OOPS! report does not imply logical consistency
edges.resolution_rule: run both; neither substitutes for the other

edges.why_related: both relate this ontology to external resources but at different stages (build-time vs integration)
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating alignment as a substitute for reuse misses build-time savings
edges.example: the same external ontology may be both reused and later aligned
edges.resolution_rule: reuse early; align later for resources not directly importable

conflict_axes.trigger: richer axioms improve modeling fidelity but raise reasoning complexity
resolution_order: profile the required inferences and ontology size
choose the least-expressive profile that supports needed axioms
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: tractable reasoning at required scale dominates; drop axioms that exceed the budget unless they are essential to a CQ
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if no profile satisfies both essential axioms and the performance budget
conflict_axes.example: prefer OWL 2 EL for a 100k-class ontology even though some DL axioms are dropped

conflict_axes.trigger: reuse improves interoperability but imports foreign commitments; building bespoke fits the domain but costs more and isolates
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: reuse dominates when a fit resource exists; build bespoke only when reuse fails a CQ-fitness or commitment check
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a reused resource forces an ontological commitment that conflicts with the domain
conflict_axes.example: reusing schema.org vs minting domain-specific product terms

conflict_axes.trigger: committing to BFO/DOLCE aids integration but adds cost and rigidity; staying lightweight is fast but limits interoperability
resolution_order: check if partners require a shared top-level
commit only if integration value exceeds cost
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: interoperability requirements dominate; commit to an upper ontology only when cross-domain integration is an intended use
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when no partner needs a shared top-level yet one is proposed anyway
conflict_axes.example: forcing BFO on a standalone internal glossary

conflict_axes.trigger: automation scales population and matching but injects noise that can break inference
resolution_order: route low-confidence items to human review
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: correctness dominates throughput; never commit automated axioms/correspondences that fail consistency or human spot-check
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if automated additions drop precision below the agreed threshold
conflict_axes.example: a matcher's high-recall equivalence set merges distinct concepts

conflict_axes.trigger: shipping faster competes with resolving every logical defect and pitfall
resolution_order: justify or defer only low-severity pitfalls
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: consistency and high-severity quality dominate speed; no release with unsatisfiable classes or critical pitfalls
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a deadline pressures shipping an inconsistent ontology
conflict_axes.example: skipping a reasoner run to meet a sprint date

conflict_axes.trigger: evolving the model competes with keeping IRIs and semantics stable for existing consumers
resolution_order: assess downstream impact of a change
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: stability for existing consumers dominates; deprecate-not-delete and never reuse a retired IRI
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a desired refactor would break existing dataset references
conflict_axes.example: renaming a class IRI that external datasets already reference

conflict_axes.trigger: deep axiomatization of few areas competes with broad coverage of all CQs
resolution_order: cover all CQs at minimum depth first
deepen axioms only where a CQ demands inference
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: CQ coverage dominates depth; do not over-axiomatize a corner while a required CQ is unanswered
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if effort spent deepening one module leaves other CQs uncovered
conflict_axes.example: heavily axiomatizing a niche subtree while core queries fail

conflict_axes.trigger: a lightweight taxonomy is cheaper but a heavyweight axiomatized ontology enables inference the use case may need
resolution_order: match artifact weight to intended use
escalate if stakeholders disagree on needed power
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: intended use dominates; build the lightest artifact that satisfies the CQs and intended inferences
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if stakeholders demand heavy axioms the use cases do not require
conflict_axes.example: axiomatizing a glossary that is only ever browsed

conflict_axes.trigger: general reusable modeling competes with precise domain-specific modeling
resolution_order: separate reusable modules from domain specifics
keep domain precision in domain modules
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: domain fidelity dominates within domain modules; generality is preferred only in shared reusable modules
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a generic pattern erases a distinction the domain requires
conflict_axes.example: collapsing two domain-distinct roles into one generic participant role

edge_cases.trigger: conflicting restriction axioms make a class unsatisfiable
edge_cases.failure_mode: class can never have instances; defined-class classification breaks
edge_cases.example: reasoner marks a class as equivalent to owl:Nothing
edge_cases.detection_method: run a DL reasoner and inspect the unsatisfiable-class list
resolution: isolate the conflicting axioms via explanation

edge_cases.trigger: importing a resource pulls a huge transitive import closure
edge_cases.failure_mode: reasoning slows or runs out of memory; unwanted axioms enter
edge_cases.example: import closure axiom count exceeds a threshold
edge_cases.detection_method: measure import-closure size and reasoner load
resolution: replace owl:imports with a minimal module extraction

edge_cases.trigger: a retired IRI is reassigned to a new concept
edge_cases.failure_mode: downstream data silently refers to the wrong concept
edge_cases.example: an IRI minted in a new release matches a previously deprecated IRI
edge_cases.detection_method: diff IRIs across releases against the deprecation registry
resolution: mint a fresh IRI for the new concept

edge_cases.trigger: a part-of relation is modeled as subClassOf
edge_cases.failure_mode: reasoner derives false subsumptions and wrong instance classifications
edge_cases.example: a subClassOf chain encodes mereological (part-whole) rather than taxonomic relations
edge_cases.detection_method: review subClassOf axioms against intended is-a semantics
resolution: replace subClassOf with a partOf object property
add the partOf property with proper characteristics

edge_cases.trigger: an automatic matcher asserts a wrong owl:equivalentClass
edge_cases.failure_mode: two distinct concepts are merged, corrupting integrated queries
edge_cases.example: an accepted equivalence introduces inconsistency or merges disjoint classes
edge_cases.detection_method: run consistency after applying alignments; spot-check high-impact equivalences
resolution: downgrade equivalence to subClassOf or skos:closeMatch

edge_cases.trigger: coverage declared without executing test queries
edge_cases.failure_mode: claimed coverage hides gaps; ontology fails in use
edge_cases.example: a CQ has a 'covered' status but no recorded query result
edge_cases.detection_method: require an executed query result per CQ before marking covered
resolution: write and run the missing test query

edge_cases.trigger: axioms exceed the chosen OWL profile
edge_cases.failure_mode: the ontology silently leaves the profile; profile-specific reasoners reject it
edge_cases.example: a profile validator reports axioms outside the declared profile
edge_cases.detection_method: run an OWL profile checker against the ontology
resolution: or escalate to a more expressive profile with cost analysis

edge_cases.trigger: learned/extracted axioms are committed without curation
edge_cases.failure_mode: false assertions corrupt inference and degrade trust
edge_cases.example: committed additions lack a confidence score or review flag
edge_cases.detection_method: require confidence scoring and review status on all learned additions
resolution: review above-threshold items, drop the rest

edge_cases.failure_mode: import resolution and reasoning become unstable or non-terminating
edge_cases.example: the import graph contains a directed cycle

edge_cases.trigger: documentation lags the released ontology version
edge_cases.failure_mode: reusers act on wrong definitions and structure
edge_cases.example: documentation version differs from the ontology version
edge_cases.detection_method: compare doc metadata version to the ontology version on release
resolution: regenerate documentation from the current ontology

edge_cases.trigger: modeling expands beyond the agreed scope
edge_cases.failure_mode: effort spent on out-of-scope concepts; CQs misaligned
edge_cases.example: classes appear with no traceable CQ or scope justification
edge_cases.detection_method: trace each class to a CQ or scope statement item
resolution: update the ORSD and re-validate traceability

edge_cases.trigger: an evidence or metric label claims more certainty than the source supports
edge_cases.failure_mode: governance trust is undermined; heuristic values appear as observed
edge_cases.example: a non-heuristic label appears without an eligible source record
edge_cases.detection_method: scan all labels against source_registry eligibility

workflow.objective: fix scope, intended uses, stakeholders, methodology, and build-vs-reuse framing
entry_criteria: domain documents and existing systems available
acceptance_tests: ORSD names intended uses and stakeholders
methodology mapped to scope

handoff_artifact.required_contents: ORSD; scope statement; intended uses; methodology; lifecycle plan

workflow.do_first_because: scope and methodology are the highest-coupling foundations every later step depends on

workflow.objective: formalize competency questions and decide which resources to reuse
acceptance_tests: each CQ answerable by a planned query
reuse decisions justified against CQs

handoff_artifact.required_contents: CQ set; CQ-to-requirement trace; reuse set; reuse fitness report

workflow.do_first_because: CQs are functional requirements and reuse fitness criteria for all modeling

workflow.objective: decide upper-ontology commitment and document ontological choices
acceptance_tests: upper-ontology choice justified against interoperability targets
commitments documented and consistent

handoff_artifact.required_contents: upper-ontology decision; ontological commitment record; top-level alignment plan

workflow.do_first_because: the top-level commitment is high-irreversibility and constrains the whole class hierarchy

workflow.objective: produce the shared conceptualization and select applicable design patterns
acceptance_tests: each concept has a reviewed informal definition
patterns match documented problems

handoff_artifact.required_contents: concept list; informal definitions; candidate relations; pattern usage record

workflow.do_first_because: agreeing concepts before formalization prevents reopening definitions during axiomatization

workflow.objective: build the class taxonomy, properties, and logical restriction axioms
acceptance_tests: subClassOf chains acyclic and meaningful
axioms trace to CQs or commitments

handoff_artifact.required_contents: class hierarchy; disjointness axioms; properties; restriction axioms

workflow.do_first_because: the TBox must stabilize before language choice, population, and reasoning

workflow.objective: set module structure, IRI policy, and representation language/profile
acceptance_tests: import graph acyclic and minimal
chosen profile supports all axioms
IRI policy guarantees persistence

handoff_artifact.required_contents: module decomposition; import graph; IRI policy; language/profile decision

workflow.do_first_because: IRI policy is high-irreversibility; fixing it before publication prevents identifier churn

workflow.objective: populate instances and curate ontology-learning outputs against the stable TBox
acceptance_tests: learned additions confidence-scored and reviewed
populated ABox passes a consistency spot-check

handoff_artifact.required_contents: populated ABox; curated learned axioms; extraction provenance; confidence scores

workflow.do_first_because: population must follow a stable TBox so instances are not invalidated by schema change

workflow.objective: run the reasoner for consistency and scan for pitfalls; route defects to repair
acceptance_tests: ontology consistent with no unsatisfiable classes
all critical pitfalls resolved or justified

handoff_artifact.required_contents: consistency report; unsatisfiable list; pitfall report; defect resolutions

workflow.do_first_because: logical and quality defects must be caught before coverage evaluation and release

workflow.objective: evaluate competency-question coverage and curate external alignments
acceptance_tests: every CQ has an executed test query with a result
each accepted correspondence is human-validated

handoff_artifact.required_contents: CQ coverage report; accuracy results; curated alignment; validation report

workflow.do_first_because: functional fitness must be demonstrated before publication and governance lock

workflow.objective: document, publish, and place the validated ontology under change control
acceptance_tests: every class/property has a label and definition
versioning and deprecation policy applied

handoff_artifact.required_contents: annotated ontology; HTML docs; metadata+license; version+deprecation policy; change log

workflow.do_first_because: hard lock only after consistency, coverage, documentation, and human review all pass

dominance_rules.trigger: a change speeds delivery but risks logical correctness or interoperability
dominance_rules.rule: never accept a delivery shortcut that fails consistency or alignment correctness
dominance_rules.example: skip the reasoner run to ship faster, rejected after an unsatisfiable class was found

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is scheduled before its unmet prerequisites
dominance_rules.rule: respect dependency precedence over raw importance ordering
dominance_rules.example: axiomatizing before properties exist forces axiom rewrites

dominance_rules.trigger: a numeric value carries a label stronger than its source supports
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade the label to heuristic or add an eligible source
dominance_rules.example: labeling a guessed coverage figure as observed without a dataset

dominance_rules.trigger: an artifact is proposed for lock before evaluation passes
dominance_rules.required_action: hold lock until OE_CONSISTENCY and OE_CQ_COVERAGE pass
dominance_rules.example: hard-locking a release before CQ coverage was measured

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or high-risk decision is about to be automated
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for irreversible/high-risk decisions
dominance_rules.required_action: require human sign-off and a decision record
dominance_rules.example: auto-committing an owl:equivalentClass alignment that merges two concepts

dominance_rules.trigger: adding more entities competes with schema/structural stability
dominance_rules.rule: schema and structural stability dominate raw volume
dominance_rules.required_action: freeze the TBox before bulk population
dominance_rules.example: mass-importing instances before disjointness axioms are settled

dominance_rules.trigger: output formatting/readability competes with strict JSON validity
dominance_rules.rule: strict JSON validity dominates prose quality
dominance_rules.example: adding explanatory comments that would break strict JSON

dominance_rules.trigger: an unsupported claim is asserted without a source
dominance_rules.required_action: attach an eligible evidence_ref or remove the claim
dominance_rules.example: asserting a benchmark number with no source record

dominance_rules.trigger: density growth threatens output completeness/context budget
dominance_rules.required_action: reduce weak similarity edges and examples first
dominance_rules.example: adding redundant near-duplicate nodes that risk truncation

dominance_rules.trigger: a locally optimal step would cause downstream rework
dominance_rules.required_action: sequence per dependency and irreversibility order
dominance_rules.example: finalizing IRIs before module structure stabilizes

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient dependency would create a cycle
dominance_rules.required_action: convert the weaker dependency to sequence or feedback
dominance_rules.example: a coverage->concept feedback kept as feedback, not a dependency cycle

dominance_rules.trigger: an object is created without traceable justification
dominance_rules.required_action: require each class/axiom to trace to a CQ or commitment
dominance_rules.example: removing a class that traces to no CQ or scope item

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve scope and intended uses before any modeling
anti_rework_rules.rationale: modeling on wrong scope forces full restructuring
anti_rework_rules.example: classes authored then dropped after scope showed they were out of scope

anti_rework_rules.rule: formalize competency questions before populating the schema
anti_rework_rules.rationale: modeling without CQs builds concepts never queried
anti_rework_rules.example: modeling a subtree that no CQ ever exercises

anti_rework_rules.rule: define the source registry before assigning evidence labels
anti_rework_rules.rationale: labels without sources cannot be validated
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a non-heuristic label with no source record
anti_rework_rules.example: an observed label appearing with no dataset

anti_rework_rules.rule: evaluate reuse before authoring new concepts
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: new concept duplicates a reusable one
anti_rework_rules.example: minting a Person class when FOAF Person was available

anti_rework_rules.rule: settle the upper-ontology commitment before finalizing the class hierarchy
anti_rework_rules.rationale: changing the top-level later re-parents the whole hierarchy
anti_rework_rules.example: retrofitting BFO categories after the hierarchy was built

anti_rework_rules.rule: define classes before fixing property domains and ranges
anti_rework_rules.rationale: properties on missing classes leave dangling domains/ranges

anti_rework_rules.rule: define properties before authoring restriction axioms
anti_rework_rules.rationale: axioms referencing missing properties require rewrites
anti_rework_rules.example: a someValuesFrom on hasPart before hasPart exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: stabilize the TBox before population and learning
anti_rework_rules.rationale: populating before schema stabilizes invalidates instances
anti_rework_rules.example: instances turn inconsistent after a late disjointness axiom

anti_rework_rules.rule: run consistency checking before measuring CQ coverage
anti_rework_rules.rationale: coverage on an inconsistent ontology is meaningless
anti_rework_rules.example: an inconsistent ontology entails everything, faking coverage

anti_rework_rules.rule: pass evaluation (consistency, pitfalls, coverage) before hard lock
publish documented release before activating governance
anti_rework_rules.rationale: governing an undocumented release leaves consumers blind
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: governance applied to an undocumented artifact
anti_rework_rules.example: versioning a release whose docs are missing

anti_rework_rules.rule: build the glossary before final concept deduplication
anti_rework_rules.rationale: deduplication without a glossary misses homonyms/synonyms
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: duplicate concepts survive into the model
anti_rework_rules.example: two terms for one concept remain as separate classes

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or evaluation reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and severity
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defects ranked first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: defect queue ordered and no high-risk defect unranked

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect or change touches locked or high-coupling nodes
acceptance_tests: all dependents identified
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set stable across two passes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect needs a repair owner
iteration_protocol.detection: map failure type to a subsystem via repair_routing
acceptance_tests: each defect has an owner

iteration_protocol.trigger: a repair changed locked or high-coupling components
acceptance_tests: no regressions vs prior pass
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: validation passes with no new failures

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or repeated failure changes a node's importance
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed within tolerance

iteration_protocol.trigger: a dependency edge creates a cycle or a conflict is mislabeled
acceptance_tests: dependency graph acyclic
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no cycles and no dependency-conflict conflation

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream node changed after a downstream lock
acceptance_tests: no stale hard lock remains
reviewer assigned and decision recorded

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new KB version is produced
acceptance_tests: no metric regressions

checks.expected: each node refs a CQ; refs resolve
no conflict edges; conflicts modeled as conflict_axes

checks.repair_action: converted coverage->concept and reasoner->axioms relations to feedback edges
recomputed all derived fields from base metrics via formula script

checks.expected: links sources, CQs, nodes, edges, workflow, validation, artifacts

version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked structural change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
downgrade alignments when a matched ontology version changes
